---
title: "Development"
---

For changes to JAXCMR itself, start with [Developer Setup](developer-setup.ipynb)
to obtain the checkout and environment. Run the commands below from the repository
root.

## Run the tests

Install the test dependencies alongside the default development tools, then run
the complete suite:

```{.bash code-summary="(1) Install test dependencies and run the suite"}
uv sync --locked --extra test
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest
```

While editing, run the relevant test file:

```{.bash code-summary="(2) Run a focused test file"}
uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/test_transitions.py
```

The complete run includes scientific regressions, package installation and
notebook execution checks. Installation checks require internet access and create
temporary environments. Run the full suite before submitting changes. The
[CI workflow](https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr/blob/main/.github/workflows/tests.yml)
defines the supported check platforms.

The [historical test-suite audit](https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr/blob/0fe217a1eb9876b013d2de01d4febfeda9b9765b/testing-audit.json)
records the earlier suite consolidation.

## Add or change a test

- Each new scenario must catch an incorrect behavior that existing scenarios do not.
- Prefer independently established numerical answers and supported workflows over
  checks of shapes or types alone.
- Keep expected answers beside their scenarios. Share fixtures where they reduce
  duplication; see the [fixture documentation](https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr/blob/main/tests/fixtures/README.md).
- Expose independent scenarios through parametrization instead of hiding them in loops.
- Required checks must not silently skip because private data is missing.

## Edit the documentation

Edit the sources; the build prepares notebook copies, downloads and HTML:

| Material | Authoritative location |
|---|---|
| Published templates | `templates/` |
| Website pages and supporting examples | `guide/` |
| Generated notebook copies and downloads | `guide/templates/`, `guide/downloads/` |
| Rendered website | `docs/` |

`guide/_quarto.yml` selects the published pages and defines the site navigation.
The render list excludes notebook downloads and supporting examples from the
published pages. Install [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/download/) 1.10.20 or
newer, then render the website:

```{.bash code-summary="(3) Render the documentation"}
bash build-docs.sh
```

This command prepares notebook pages before Quarto discovers the render targets,
so it also works in a fresh checkout. It refreshes downloads, removes retired
staging files and clears the generated website output without executing notebook
cells. Execute changed notebooks separately and retain their
useful outputs before rendering. Do not edit the generated copies.

Open `docs/index.html`, or start a live preview:

```{.bash code-summary="(4) Preview the documentation"}
quarto preview guide
```

After editing an original notebook in `templates/`, run `bash build-docs.sh` again: live preview
does not watch those files outside the guide project. Review the rendered pages
and notebook downloads locally before publication. Colab links and package
installation follow `main`. GitHub Pages publishes the committed `docs/` directory.
